Name: Apache Tomcat RCE Vulnerability (Mar 2025) - Linux
description: Apache Tomcat is prone to a remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability.
detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host.
insight: The original implementation of partial PUT used a temporary le based on the user provided le name and path with the path separator replaced by '.'.

If all of the following are true, a malicious user is able to view security sensitive les and/or inject content into those les: - writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default) - support for partial PUT (enabled by default) - a target URL for security sensitive uploads that is a sub-directory of a target URL for public uploads - attacker knowledge of the names of security sensitive les being uploaded - the security sensitive les also being uploaded via partial PUT

If all of the following are true, a malicious user is able to perform remote code execution: - writes enabled for the default servlet (disabled by default) - support for partial PUT (enabled by default) - application is using Tomcat's le based session persistence with the default storage location - application includes a library that may be leveraged in a deserialization attack

description: Apache Tomcat is prone to a denial of service vulnerability in the HTTP/2 implementation.
detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host.
Details: Apache Tomcat DoS Vulnerability (Mar 2019) - Linux
Version used: 2025-09-16T05:38:45Z
Product Detection Result: Product: cpe:/a:apache:tomcat:8.5.23
Method: Apache Tomcat Detection Consolidation (OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.107652)
impact: Server-side threads can be exhausted by clients keeping streams open or sending excessive SETTINGS frames, resulting in denial of service.
solution: VendorFix: Update to version 8.5.38, 9.0.16 or later.
insight: The HTTP/2 implementation accepts streams with excessive numbers of SETTINGS frames and permits clients to keep streams open without reading/writing request/response data.
By keeping streams open for requests that utilise the Servlet API's blocking I/O, clients are able to cause server-side threads to block eventually leading to thread exhaustion and a DoS.

Product detection method: Apache Tomcat Detection Consolidation (OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.107652)
impact: Possible authentication bypass or weakened authentication allowing users to authenticate using variations of their user name and/or bypass some LockOut Realm protections.
insight: Queries made by the JNDI Realm do not always correctly escape parameters.
Parameter values could be sourced from user provided data (eg user names) as well as configuration data provided by an administrator.
In limited circumstances it is possible for users to authenticate using variations of their user name and/or to bypass some of the protection provided by the LockOut Realm.

Details: Apache Tomcat Information Disclosure Vulnerability (Mar 2023) - Linux OID:1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.104653 Version used: 2024-06-07T05:05:42Z
impact: Information disclosure: session cookies may be transmitted over an insecure channel if the secure attribute is not set when proxied via HTTP with X-Forwarded-Proto set to https.
insight: When using the RemoteIpFilter with requests received from a reverse proxy via HTTP that include the X-Forwarded-Proto header set to https, session cookies created by Tomcat did not include the secure attribute. This could result in the user agent transmitting the session cookie over an insecure channel.

Name: ICMP Timestamp Reply Information Disclosure
description: The remote host responded to an ICMP timestamp request.
detection_result: The following response / ICMP packet has been received:
detection_method: Sends an ICMP Timestamp (Type 13) request and checks if a Timestamp Reply (Type 14) is received.
impact: This information could theoretically be used to exploit weak time-based random number generators in other services.
solution: Disable the support for ICMP timestamp on the remote host completely
Protect the remote host by a rewall, and block ICMP packets passing through the rewall in either direction (either completely or only for untrusted networks)
insight: The Timestamp Reply is an ICMP message which replies to a Timestamp message. It consists of the originating timestamp sent by the sender of the Timestamp as well as a receive timestamp and a transmit timestamp.

Name: Apache Tomcat Information Disclosure Vulnerability (Sep 2022) - Linux
description: Apache Tomcat is prone to an information disclosure vulnerability.
detection_result: Detected by Apache Tomcat Detection Consolidation (OID: 1.3.6.1.4.1.25623.1.0.10 ->7652)
detection_method: Checks if a vulnerable version is present on the target host.
impact: A concurrency bug could cause client connections to share an Http11Processor instance resulting in responses, or part responses, to be received by the wrong client, leading to information disclosure.
insight: The simplied implementation of blocking reads and writes introduced in Tomcat 10 and back-ported to Tomcat 9.0.47 onwards exposed a long standing (but extremely hard to trigger) concurrency bug that could cause client connections to share an Http11Processor instance resulting in responses, or part responses, to be received by the wrong client.
